elements.element: Customer indemnity limited to Customer's breach of law

elements.evidence: "(a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe ... any intellectual property right"

elements.element: Vendor indemnity subject to super-cap of 3× annual fees
elements.evidence: No cap text; "21. LIMITATION OF LIABILITY" untouched.

reasons: All preferred atomic elements are present: Vendor defend-and-indemnify running to Customer and Affiliates, the four trigger categories (IP infringement of Services/Deliverables, Vendor breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Customer Data incident, gross negligence/wilful misconduct), and the three procedural mechanics (prompt written notice, control of defence, reasonable cooperation).

The reciprocal Customer indemnity in 20.1 is properly narrowed from "every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services" to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of Applicable Law, matching the preferred limitation.

Fallback is incomplete (no modification/combination/specification exclusions, no procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, no 3× annual fees super-cap), but that is irrelevant since the locked preferred level is fully satisfied and levels are not combined.

Minimality holds: one targeted replacement of the one-sided Customer indemnity plus a concise insertion supplying the absent Vendor indemnity; no hold-harmless expansion, extra indemnitees, settlement mechanics, or fallback remedies were imported.

Intent preserved: all defined terms used (Affiliates, Applicable Law, Customer Data, Deliverables, Services) are resolved, numbering runs 20.1–20.3, and clause 21 is untouched with no dangling cross-reference.
